cells.tense: You are in the clearing after an ending, and the pull of what might come is wide open.
cells.ask: Name out loud which two pulls belong to the thing that ended, and which stand on their own.
cells.core:
Something ended. A lot of wanting is arriving at once — projects, people, places, all of it glowing a little. That isn't you being scattered. The ending made room, and now you're seeing what could go in it.

What's working is that you haven't grabbed the first thing that glowed. The ending stays an ending and the pull stays a pull long enough for you to see how many kinds are here. Sort two of them before you move on either: this one came from what finished, this one didn't. Pulling toward something is fine while you sort it. It gets murky when you've acted and can't say why.

cells.tense: You are treating the ending as a door you are about to walk through, and living past it already.
cells.ask: Finish one clearing still sitting half-done today — the box, the message, the last of it — before you look at what's next.
cells.core:
The ending isn't finished and you're already past it. Every pull of what might come gets treated as something to decide on now — one more feeling gathered, one more maybe held open, because closing this seems to cost something you haven't priced yet.

But you can't see what's next while you're holding all of it up. The ending is the frame, and you're standing outside it, braced for a morning that hasn't arrived. One actual end, fully done, and the pull stops being an emergency. Then whatever is still pulling can be felt at its own pace instead of at the pace of your not knowing.

cells.tense: You stopped gathering what could be felt, and the ending behind you has stayed the last thing you reached toward.
cells.ask: Put one thing you are drawn to where you will see it tomorrow — a note, a tab, the object itself — and leave it there unanswered.
cells.core:
There is an ending behind you. The clearing itself went through, and the pull is not moving. The draws are still there; they just sit on your side of the door, and nothing in front of you looks like a maybe anymore. When something good comes up in you, it doesn't go anywhere.

Start smaller than choosing. One thing you like, left where you'll pass it again, with no decision attached. That gives the pull somewhere to land without asking you to want it out loud. The ending already happened. This is only checking whether reaching toward something is still available to you.

cells.tense: You are already drawn toward several possible futures, and you are describing it as just seeing what happens.
cells.ask: Write down the one pull you keep coming back to, tell one person it is yours, and stop calling it a coincidence.
cells.core:
People can feel it. You get pulled — a project, a person, a place — and there's a low hum in you that has already gone toward something. You call it being open to what comes. But you are not neutral. It's happening, and you're not in the sentence about it.

That matters because the ending was yours too. You cleared the space, and now something is gathering in it. Naming what you're already pulled toward costs nothing and makes the next move possible — yours, not the room's. The pull isn't a mood that happens to you; it's evidence about what you actually want.
cells.sheetLine: You are already choosing. You are just calling it openness.

attempts.check: The record does not say the person is choosing endings; it says the card gathers emotional possibilities where something is ending, so any line that treats the endings as already handled, or the feeling as already picked, is mine and not the record's. A reader could reasonably say the ending is not theirs at all — it was handed to them — and the ask still works if that is true, because saying out loud what the pull is attached to is useful either way. The sentence that would serve me more than them is anything tidy about 'the harvest', which sounds like the ending is a promise rather than a clear-out; it is cut from every cell.
